name: audio.process
title: Process audio (pitch, tempo, trim, fades)
summary: Run an ordered list of processing steps over audio takes: ffmpeg filters, pitch, tempo, gain, silence trim, pause tightening, fades and peak normalisation, written as wav, flac or mp3, with each file's audible onset and peak time.
description: The voice-fx and cleanup pass, for one file or a batch of takes. Each step does exactly one thing and the steps run in the order given, so a take can be pitched down for a deeper voice, its long pauses tightened, its edges faded and its peak normalised in one job. With no steps and no conversion options a file is only re-encoded. Presets such as deep-hero carry a whole named chain; a request's own steps replace a preset's steps. A step that needs real DSP is an ffmpeg chain, so it appears in the result's chain list in the order it ran; gain, trim, tightening, fades and normalisation are done in memory and do not add a chain. Every output reports `onset_s` (where the file first becomes audible, at or above -30 dBFS, or null when silent) and `peak_at_s` (the time of the sample peak), so a cue can be lined up on the frame where the sound actually starts. Nothing is enforced: no normalisation, no trimming, no resampling unless asked.

inputs.description: Audio files to process, in order. Each becomes one output; the same stem twice gets a -2/-3 suffix.

items.description: One audio file: a workspace path, job:<id>/<output> or pin:<name>. Its first audio stream is processed.

preset.description: Name of a preset under presets/audio-process/ (deep-hero, uncanny-villain) whose values are merged under this request. Your own fields win; your own steps replace the preset's steps.

steps.description: Processing steps, applied in order. Each step object holds exactly one operation. Empty means: just decode and re-encode.

items.description: One operation: filter, pitch_semitones, tempo, gain_db, trim_silence, tighten_pauses, fade_in_s, fade_out_s or normalize_peak_db.

filter.description: An ffmpeg -af chain applied as-is, e.g. "highpass=f=90,acompressor=threshold=0.06" or "bass=g=5:f=110,volume=6dB". File-reading filters (movie, amovie, sendcmd, zmq) are refused.

pitch_semitones.description: Shift the pitch by this many semitones (negative = deeper) while keeping the duration. Runs as asetrate + aresample + atempo.

tempo.description: Speed factor with the pitch kept: 2 plays twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast. Duration is divided by it.

gain_db.description: Multiply the amplitude by this many dB (positive louder, negative quieter). No limiter: integer output formats clip above 0 dBFS.

trim_silence.description: Remove leading and/or trailing audio below threshold_db, judged by the peak over all channels, keeping keep_s of it.

threshold_db.description: Frames whose peak over all channels is at or below this dBFS count as silence.

start.description: Trim the silent head of the file.

end.description: Trim the silent tail of the file.

keep_s.description: Seconds of the silence to keep at each trimmed edge (30 ms by default).

tighten_pauses.description: Shorten every internal pause longer than max_pause_s to exactly max_pause_s, keeping half of it on each side of the cut. Leading and trailing silence are left alone.

max_pause_s.description: Longest pause to keep, in seconds. Every longer internal silence is cut down to this. Required.

threshold_db.description: A window is silent when its peak over all channels is below this dBFS.

window_ms.description: Length of the analysis window in milliseconds. 10 ms is the dialogue-editor default.

fade_in_s.description: Linear fade in from silence over this many seconds at the start.

fade_out_s.description: Linear fade out to silence over this many seconds at the end.

normalize_peak_db.description: Scale the whole file so its absolute sample peak lands exactly at this dBFS (0 = full scale). Rounded/actual peak may differ by the rounding of the output format.

format.description: Output format: wav = 16-bit, wav24, wav32f = 32-bit float (no clipping), flac, mp3 (192 kbit/s).

sample_rate.description: Convert the output to this sample rate in Hz. Omit to keep the input rate.

channels.description: Convert the output to this channel count (1 = mono, 2 = stereo). Omit to keep the input's channel count.
